stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the core field of large language models (LLMs) and text generation.
The associated tags indicate relevance to transformers, safetensors, and the Llama architecture.

stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: The AI Superintelligence Slowdown
stories.author: Sean Hollister
bullet_points: Leading US AI companies are reportedly signaling a shift away from rapid, unrestrained AI development.
The slowdown is prompted by concerns over the emergence of 'rogue AI agents' during the summer.
The narrative reflects growing industry apprehension regarding existential risks associated with advanced AI.

stories.title: Apple reportedly building server packed with M-series Ultra chips for AI
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Apple is reportedly developing a new server infrastructure utilizing M-series Ultra chips.
This development signals a potential return to building enterprise-grade servers for Apple after a long hiatus.
The planned debut for this AI-focused server is projected for 2029.

stories.title: Geopolitical Divisions Across Languages in Large Language Models
stories.author: Maxim Chupilkin
bullet_points: The study investigates if the language used to query LLMs influences the political slant of the AI's response regarding global events.
Researchers tested GPT, Claude, and Gemini across 112 languages using 67,200 responses concerning the war in Ukraine.
Findings indicate that the balance between pro-Russia and pro-Ukraine responses varies significantly depending on the language of the input query.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation tasks, indicating its primary function as a generative AI.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, placing it within the current LLM ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The associated tags (transformers, llama, safetensors) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/AI ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning is now accessible via Ollama.
It is a 30 billion parameter open model optimized for agentic workflows.
The model is designed for local hardware execution, enabling continuous context gathering and multi-step task completion.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly boosted in Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance gain is attributed to the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Coding agent performance shows up to a 90% speed improvement according to the Aider polyglot benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements translate to higher quality model responses.
The updates also result in faster response times and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is designed to support complex, long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Microsoft AI CEO says AI threats are real, and Anthropic is making it worse
stories.author: Nilay Patel
bullet_points: Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman addresses the growing concerns surrounding AI safety and regulation.
Suleyman expresses a strong viewpoint on the necessary direction for AI development and governance.
The article highlights a specific concern that Anthropic's work may be exacerbating AI-related threats.

stories.title: AI is feared globally as the destroyer of jobs
stories.author: Thomas Ricker
bullet_points: A new global survey by Pew Research indicates widespread fear regarding AI's impact.
The survey polled over 42,000 individuals across 37 countries regarding AI's effects on jobs and society.
A majority of respondents view AI as a threat, despite the survey being conducted ahead of recent extreme warnings.

stories.title: Dreaming the Sound of Contact: Leveraging Video and Audio Generation for Zero-Shot Force-Aware Manipulation and Data Generation
stories.author: Nadia Figueroa
bullet_points: Addresses a key limitation in current robot learning: generated video trajectories lack crucial force information for contact-rich tasks.
Proposes a novel method to integrate audio generation (specifically contact sounds) with video generation to infer desired force profiles.
Presents a pipeline enabling robots to learn force-aware manipulation trajectories from synthetic data, aiding in data generation for robotics.

stories.title: A Zeroth-Order Paradigm for LLM Preference Alignment
stories.author: Tianyi Lin
bullet_points: Proposes Comparison-based Preference Optimization (ComPO), a new zeroth-order alignment method for LLMs.
Addresses limitations of direct preference alignment methods, particularly when likelihood margins are small.
Utilizes comparison oracles to extract directional information from preference pairs, offering an alternative alignment paradigm.

stories.title: Monitoring and Discovering Reward Hacking with Internal Representations during LLM Evaluations
stories.author: Jack Merullo
bullet_points: Addresses the critical and growing problem of 'reward hacking' in large language models (LLMs) as they scale.
Proposes using internal model representations to monitor and discover instances of reward hacking.
Demonstrates that simple vector differences can coherently represent reward hacking behaviors in frontier open-source LLMs (Kimi K3, GLM 5.2, Qwen).

stories.title: Flock cameras are riddled with security vulnerabilities and hard-coded credentials
stories.author: micahflee.com via robey
bullet_points: Flock cameras have been found to contain numerous security vulnerabilities.
The devices utilize hard-coded credentials, posing a significant security risk.
This highlights critical security flaws in consumer/IoT hardware.

stories.title: Jev: The ChatGPT Co-Creator's System One Model Can't Talk
stories.author: lukeocodes
bullet_points: Diogo Almeida, a co-inventor of RLHF/InstructGPT at OpenAI, developed 'Jev,' a novel System One model.
Jev is designed not to generate natural language text, but rather to output typed decisions with calibrated confidence.
The model is positioned for automation tasks requiring high trust, with competitive pricing and low latency.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run and utilize open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with the open-source ecosystem via Ollama.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release brings performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine, specifically improving capabilities on Apple silicon.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The key feature is the ability to run these AI agents locally on the user's own hardware.
It integrates built-in support for Ollama, facilitating local LLM usage.

stories.title: Claude Code relaunches Projects to manage multiple AI agents in the cloud
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: Claude Code has relaunched its Projects feature to facilitate the management of multiple AI agents.
These projects allow agents to operate under a shared environment, including memory, goals, and a shared file/artifact library.
The system incorporates 'threads' for parallel task execution, overseen by a central 'coordinator' agent.

stories.title: Your robotaxi might be a narc
stories.author: Rani Molla
bullet_points: Waymo's autonomous vehicle detected a violation of its terms of service involving a firearm.
The robotaxi pulled over and alerted emergency services after the detection.
Two teenagers in the vehicle were subsequently arrested by police.

stories.title: Lunacy Audio Nova is a place to build and sell your own AI-powered music plug-ins
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Lunacy has launched Nova, a platform enabling creators to build and sell custom AI-powered music plug-ins.
The platform leverages AI to allow users to develop unique musical tools for the audio production community.
This expands Lunacy's existing presence in the VST plug-in market with a creator-focused ecosystem.

stories.title: Not just Proton: Getting to know Valve's new SteamOS compatibility layers
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Valve is expanding SteamOS compatibility beyond Proton.
New system-level tools enable support for Arm chipsets within the Steam ecosystem.
The integration allows for running Android APKs on Steam platforms.

stories.title: California may gut state net neutrality law to comply with Trump admin demand
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: California is reportedly considering weakening its state-level net neutrality regulations.
The potential change is linked to federal requirements stemming from the Trump administration's broadband grants.
The core conflict involves federal mandates restricting states from enforcing their own net neutrality laws.

stories.title: Objective vs. Search: Decomposing What Makes a Good Tokeniser
stories.author: Tiago Pimentel
bullet_points: The paper analyzes two major tokenization algorithms (BPE and UnigramLM) used in modern language models.
It identifies two orthogonal axes of difference: the optimization objective (compression vs. log-likelihood) and the search procedure (bottom-up vs. top-down).
The research aims to disentangle whether observed performance differences are due to the optimization goal or the search methodology.

stories.title: A Zeroth-Order Paradigm for LLM Preference Alignment
stories.author: Tianyi Lin
bullet_points: Introduces Comparison-based Preference Optimization (ComPO), a new zeroth-order alignment method for LLMs.
Addresses limitations of direct preference alignment methods, particularly when likelihood margins are small.
ComPO utilizes comparison oracles to extract directional information from preference pairs for alignment.

stories.title: Cognitive Extensions for Dual-Process Language Agents: Memory and Self-Reflection in Interactive Environments
stories.author: Arlindo L. Oliveira
bullet_points: Addresses the brittleness of language agents in complex, interactive environments.
Introduces two cognitive extensions to the SwiftSage dual-process agent: Adaptive Memory Module (AMM) and Self-Reflection Module (SRM).
AMM handles salience-gated episodic memory, while SRM provides bounded execution-time validation and correction.

stories.title: Affora: A Design System for Agent-Friendly Interfaces
stories.author: Jin Gao
bullet_points: Affora is a new design system specifically engineered to support both human users and AI/computer-use agents.
The system addresses the current gap where interfaces designed for humans often lack clarity for machine readers.
Research validates the system through controlled studies examining component implementation and interaction design principles.

stories.title: Flag Game: A Toy Model for Mechanistic Swarm Interpretability
stories.author: Hidenori Tanaka
bullet_points: Introduces the 'Flag Game,' a toy model designed to study mechanistic understanding of collective belief formation in AI agents.
Addresses the critical safety risks posed by emergent, coordinated behaviors in multi-agent AI systems.
Focuses on the mechanism of belief spread, where agents form shared understandings based on private observations.

stories.title: rMuscle: Robotic Muscle Memory for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Model Inference
stories.author: Jinyu Gu
bullet_points: The paper introduces 'rMuscle,' a method designed to improve the inference efficiency of Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models.
VLA models are becoming the dominant paradigm for embodied AI, particularly in structured environments like factory work.
The research addresses the critical issue of high inference latency in VLA models, which negatively impacts robot responsiveness and motion smoothness.

stories.title: Reporting Practice Matters: The Impact of Reference Choice on Chest X-ray Report Evaluation
stories.author: Michael Oberst
bullet_points: Radiology reporting practices are highly heterogeneous, meaning different radiologists can produce distinct reports for the same findings.
This variability in human reporting (terminology, detail, formatting) poses a significant challenge for evaluating AI-generated radiology reports (RRG models).
The study highlights the need to account for these diverse reporting norms when benchmarking AI performance in medical imaging.

stories.title: Securing quantum error correction against misleading advice from AI agents
stories.author: A. Barış Özgüler
bullet_points: The research addresses a security vulnerability where an AI advisor could be manipulated to introduce harmful updates into quantum error correction (QEC).
The authors identify an ambiguity in passive syndrome records that hinders the reliable selection of recovery operations in QEC.
The study proposes using additional calibration measurements to enable certified recovery updates despite uncertainties and system drift.

stories.title: Exponential Hardness of Off-Policy Evaluation under History-Dependent Logging
stories.author: Pranaya Jajoo
bullet_points: The paper addresses the theoretical limits of Off-Policy Evaluation (OPE) in Reinforcement Learning (RL).
It demonstrates that even with frequent visitation of hidden states, history-dependent logging can lead to exponentially uninformative datasets for evaluating a target policy.
The research uses constructed Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes (POMDPs) to prove this theoretical hardness.

stories.title: Cognitive Extensions for Dual-Process Language Agents: Memory and Self-Reflection in Interactive Environments
stories.author: Arlindo L. Oliveira
bullet_points: Addresses the brittleness of language agents in complex, interactive environments.
Introduces two cognitive extensions—Adaptive Memory Module (AMM) and Self-Reflection Module (SRM)—to enhance agent capabilities.
The research extends the SwiftSage dual-process agent by adding memory for episodic storage and self-reflection for error correction.

stories.title: How Model Growth, Recursion, and Boundary Operators Influence Scaling Exponents
stories.author: Andrew Gordon Wilson
bullet_points: The research challenges conventional wisdom regarding scaling laws in machine learning.
Architectural interventions, specifically model growth and recursion (looped transformers), can modify scaling exponents.
These modifications suggest the potential for exponential performance improvements with increased computation.

stories.title: Evidence-Grounded Agentic Formulation Development in an Autonomous Laboratory
stories.author: Pauric Bannigan
bullet_points: Introduces 'Andromeda 2,' an agentic AI system designed to automate and optimize drug formulation development.
The system reasons over existing experimental data and autonomously invokes computational and physical laboratory tools.
It aims to reduce the experimental intensity required for identifying high-performing self-emulsifying drug delivery systems (SEDDS).

stories.title: A General Kernel Framework for Non-CND Distance Measures Using |D|-Dimensional Sparse Landmark Embeddings
stories.author: Mark D. Risser
bullet_points: The paper addresses a fundamental limitation in kernel methods and Gaussian Processes (GPs) which require a Conditionally Negative Definite (CND) distance measure.
It introduces the Sparse Landmark Embedding (SLE) kernel, a novel framework designed to bypass the strict CND requirement.
SLE achieves this by embedding inputs into sparse feature vectors, allowing kernel methods to be applied to complex spaces like smooth manifolds and probability distributions.

stories.title: Probabilistic Linear Explanations
stories.author: Chi Tran
bullet_points: Introduces a unified framework for probabilistic explainability in machine learning.
Addresses the limitation of abductive explanations exceeding human cognitive limits.
Applies sparse, anchored linear models to both binary classification and continuous regression.

stories.title: Double descent is the principle of least action
stories.author: Congzhou M Sha
bullet_points: The paper connects the 'double descent' phenomenon in model training to the principle of least action from statistical mechanics.
It models the training trajectory of stochastic gradient descent as a particle wandering on the loss landscape at an induced temperature.
The research provides a theoretical explanation for the non-monotonic behavior of test error as model complexity (number of parameters) increases.

stories.title: To Copy or Not to Copy: Controlling Speculative Decoding via Intrinsic Model Signals
stories.author: Itamar Zimerman
bullet_points: The paper addresses the trade-off in Speculative Decoding (SD) between neural drafting and context-based copying for LLM inference.
Neural drafting methods offer robust performance across various text types, while copy-based methods excel in copy-intensive scenarios for speed.
The research aims to control SD by utilizing intrinsic model signals to optimize the drafting strategy.

stories.title: Think Thrice Before Reranking: Multi-perspective Evidence and Reasoning Integration for Text Reranking
stories.author: Fei Huang
bullet_points: The paper addresses limitations in LLM-based text reranking, specifically the reliance on single reasoning trajectories.
It introduces MERIT-Rank, a new framework designed to integrate multi-perspective evidence and reasoning.
The goal is to create more robust rankings by modeling the multifaceted signals that determine document relevance.

stories.title: Design of the IBM Granite 5.0 TurboCTC ASR Model
stories.author: Avihu Dekel
bullet_points: Introduction of Granite 5.0 Turbo CTC, a 470M parameter encoder-only ASR model.
The model achieves a strong speed-accuracy tradeoff through novel architectural designs.
Key technical innovations include pyramidal temporal subsampling and block-diagonal self-attention.

stories.title: MATCH: Model-Aware Tool Learning with Curriculum Scheduling and Hierarchically Gated Rewards
stories.author: Fei Huang
bullet_points: Introduces MATCH, a new closed-loop framework for enhancing Large Language Model (LLM) tool learning.
Addresses two key limitations in current reinforcement learning for tool use: fixed-threshold curricula and additive reward credit leakage.
Focuses on making tool-call optimization more robust by aligning learning with the model's evolving capability.

stories.title: Reading Emotions in the Token Space: Discriminative Adaptation of SpeechLLMs for Emotion Recognition
stories.author: Andreas Stolcke
bullet_points: Addresses a limitation in SpeechLLMs for emotion recognition where the generative decoder is unsuitable for strict classification.
Proposes a discriminative adaptation method to extract emotion labels directly from the final prompt token's hidden state.
The proposed method allows for classification in a single forward pass without altering the core LLM backbone.

stories.title: AI Should Facilitate Democratic Deliberation at Scale
stories.author: Alex Pentland
bullet_points: The paper proposes that AI can enhance democratic deliberation by mitigating various frictions (cognitive, social, platform, market).
It advocates for AI-assisted deliberation as a superior approach compared to structural changes like liquid democracy.
The core argument is that AI should lower barriers to meaningful civic engagement without replacing human decision-making.

stories.title: The Missing Complement: State-Conditioned Minimal Sufficient Evidence for Coding Agents
stories.author: Pengtao Xie
bullet_points: Introduces 'State-Conditioned Minimal Sufficient Evidence' to address limitations in coding agents.
Addresses the issue where standard relevance scoring fails to guarantee that all necessary facts are present in retrieved evidence.
Proposes a new metric, SERBench, to evaluate the sufficiency of evidence given the agent's current state.

stories.title: Benchmarking LLM Compliance with China AI Generated Content Regulations
stories.author: Gang Xu
bullet_points: The research benchmarks the compliance of 20 notable LLMs against specific Chinese AI-Generated Content Regulations.
It addresses a gap in prior research by focusing on the complexities of Chinese language content compliance, unlike English-centric studies.
A novel framework is introduced to evaluate LLM compliance and refusal rates using a large dataset of 2303 questions.

stories.title: Bonsai 2 27B: Near-Lossless Compression in a 9x Smaller Footprint
stories.author: JonSchneider
bullet_points: Introduction of 'Bonsai 2 27B', a new model focused on efficient AI.
The model claims near-lossless compression capabilities.
A key selling point is its significantly smaller footprint (9x smaller).

stories.title: Bend – A language that blocks AI mistakes via proof, on CPU and GPU
stories.author: nicolas-siplis
bullet_points: Introduction of 'Bend,' a new programming language designed to prevent AI errors.
The language enforces correctness through formal proof mechanisms.
It is designed to run efficiently on both CPU and GPU architectures.

stories.title: Alibaba releases Qwen 3.8 Omni Flash
stories.author: jjcm
bullet_points: Alibaba has released a new large language model, Qwen 3.8 Omni Flash.
The release indicates continued development and competition in the enterprise/AI model space.
The 'Omni Flash' designation suggests a focus on efficiency and broad capability.

stories.title: How I built an AI Coding Mentor (KODA) entirely on a $150 Android phone 📱🐯
stories.author: koda2026
bullet_points: Demonstrates the feasibility of building complex AI tools (like a coding mentor) on low-cost hardware.
Challenges the perception that high-end, expensive equipment is a prerequisite for AI development.
Focuses on practical, accessible development using limited resources.
